main_text.p: nec sic tamen conseqveretur, nævos in vulgata nullos esse, errores & ofcitantias nullas; seqveretur eqvidem,nihil horum ab Interprete commissum esse, sed Ama-nuenses in ea describenda nunqvam ab-errasse, cespitasse, oscitasse,qvis præstare audebit? hoc esset in hæreticorū insaniā ruere, qvi Græcos & Hebræos codices, præfertim hos posteriores, volunt eadem puritate nunc excellere,qvâ primùm fusi sunt, ut vulgata Ecclesiæ editio secundū eos absolutè corrigatur ; contra hanc hæreticorum suorum insaniam validissi-mè scripsit Capellus & prope innumeris exemplis demonstravit, in codices He-bræos plurimas mendas irrepsisse, tantū-qve abest ut vulgatæ injuriam intulerit, ut ex comparatione vulgatæ cū Hebræo textu plurimas in Hebræum textum irre-psisse mendas colligit, ut videre est lib. §[?] c. 7, 8, 9, 10, 11. nos de Græco textu idem variis modis fusè demonstravimus in Ex-ercitat. Biblicis lib. 1. tota Exercit. 2, & multis annis ante Capellum de Hebræo textu ex ipsa Masora variisqve autoribus

page.notes: Printed text is a single paragraph running over the page; it begins mid-sentence. The "§" after "lib." is a doubtful reading, possibly a section sign or a mark from the printer, and is marked [?]. Long s is given as s throughout. "insaniā" in line 7 is a doubtful final letter, which may be an á or ā. The catchword "Hebræ-" is at the foot right.
